reason: The hypothesis combines the observation from P6/P25 that coherent L12 nanoprecipitates do not pin domain walls with the general knowledge that slower cooling can coarsen precipitates and introduce interfacial dislocations, proposing that deliberately reducing coherency in the same FeCoNiTaAl system will increase coercivity. This is a straightforward inversion of the P6/P25 design principle and does not synthesize findings from multiple distinct papers or transfer an idea to a new alloy system with a novel mechanism.
copied_elements: coherent nanoprecipitates do not pin domain walls (P6, P23, P24, P25)
defects such as dislocations act as pinning centers for domain walls (P1, P2, P10)
semi-coherent interfaces with misfit dislocations exist in phase-separated HEAs (P31)
cooling rate can alter precipitate size and coherency (general knowledge)
